parameters.name: ain
parameters.description: Effective inlet conversion coefficient: `ain*flow` adds pressure from metered air. Estimated jointly with the other independent coefficients at both fitting stages described below.

parameters.name: weight
parameters.description: Fraction of open-valve conductance assigned to `1-(valve/vfull)**3`; the complement multiplies `1-3*(valve/vfull)**2+2*(valve/vfull)**3`. Both basis functions decrease with closure and vanish at the seat. Estimated jointly at both stages.

parameters.name: cap
parameters.description: Maximum small-overpressure relaxation-rate scale at the open valve. Estimated jointly with the other independent coefficients, with `0.03 <= cap <= 0.5` 1/s to make the near-atmospheric dynamics resolvable by one five-second RK4 step.

parameters.name: eps
parameters.description: Pressure scale for smoothing the ideal square-root cusp near atmosphere. Estimated jointly at both stages, with `0.01 <= eps <= 0.5` bar; this is an effective laminar/low-Reynolds-number crossover correction, not independently measured hardware.

parameters.name: gamma
parameters.description: Ideal-air ratio of specific heats, `gamma = 1.4`, assumed for room-temperature air; not fitted. NASA Glenn Research Center, Mass Flow Choking, supplies the ideal-air nozzle framework (source checked during this round).

parameters.name: rcrit
parameters.description: Critical downstream/upstream pressure ratio for an isentropic converging nozzle; below this ratio the ideal mass flux is choked.

parameters.name: gopen
parameters.description: Open-valve scale of the dimensionless compressible mass-flux function, tied to the fitted near-atmospheric rate and crossover pressure.

parameters.name: patm
parameters.description: Atmospheric reference pressure, `patm = 1` bar, supplied approximately by TASK.md and here assumed exactly; not adjusted to reduce simulation errors.

parameters.name: vfull
parameters.description: Fully closed valve normalization, `vfull = 100` %, from TASK.md. Clamping `Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)` restricts the conductance extension to the physical stroke.

parameters.name: back
parameters.description: Subatmospheric restoring rate, `back = 0.1` 1/s, chosen as a ten-second numerical vacuum-relaxation time, not estimated. `-back*Min(p-patm,0)` is a valve-independent extension outside normal pressurized operation, not an identified leak or a model of real reverse valve flow.

estimation.criterion: Final criterion: sum of squared free-run errors on pressure `p` in bar after each trajectory’s first sample, with no state correction. This matches long-horizon evaluation and avoids treating the filtered derivative `dp` as an independent instantaneous measurement. One-step pressure-transition squared error is only an initialization criterion.
estimation.data: Final coefficients use all 1452 rows of data/train.csv and all 1454 rows of data/val.csv as two separate trajectories, without joining their endpoints. There are 1451 and 1453 fitted pressure transitions. Initial samples set each free-run initial condition and are not residuals. The derivative column `dp` is not used for final estimation. The independent training-only comparison and first-two-thirds blocked comparison in fixed_atmosphere.py were used to assess structure generalization; only after these checks were both entire trajectories used to improve coefficient coverage. No rows were removed for outlier or transient handling and no test data were accessed.
estimation.method: Bound-constrained nonlinear least squares using the Trust Region Reflective algorithm in scipy.optimize.least_squares (SciPy 1.18.1). Reference: SciPy official least_squares documentation, checked in this round. Nonlinearity and physical bounds make a direct linear solution inapplicable. All four independent parameters were estimated together in each of two stages. First minimize squared one-step RK4 pressure-transition errors, starting at `ain = 0.0013` bar/(s*(l/min)), `cap = 0.35` 1/s, `eps = 0.1` bar, `weight = 0.5`; these broad positive guesses are close to preliminary mass-balance fit scales and avoid a vanishing-conductance start. That stage yielded `ain = 0.0013233398587` bar/(s*(l/min)), `cap = 0.5` 1/s, `eps = 0.0471207616966` bar, `weight = 0.613779532921`. Then, starting at those values, minimize squared full free-run pressure errors and obtain `ain = 0.00129690189646` bar/(s*(l/min)), `cap = 0.37967991473` 1/s, `eps = 0.100812285724` bar, `weight = 0.508510289395`. The numerical bounds were `0.0001 <= ain <= 0.005` bar/(s*(l/min)), `0.03 <= cap <= 0.5` 1/s, `0.01 <= eps <= 0.5` bar and `0 <= weight <= 1`. The gain is broadly positive, the crossover stays nonsingular, the weights enforce a monotone valve map, and the rate ceiling avoids an unresolved atmospheric-pressure cusp during a five-second RK4 step. Both stages use two-point finite-difference Jacobians, `x_scale = "jac"`, linear loss, and relative stopping settings `ftol = 1e-11`, `xtol = 1e-11`, `gtol = 1e-11`; maximum function evaluations were 1000 and 1500 respectively, with actual solver counts 18 and 32. Each simulation is one classical RK4 step per `Ts = 5` s with the current logged inputs held constant. Numba 0.68.0 compiles the loops; no random sampling or seeds apply. Fixed and tied parameters are not optimization variables. The function guards excursions beyond 20 bar with a finite penalty; neither final fitted training trajectory approaches that guard.

discussion.family: Lumped isothermal gas-inventory balance with regularized isentropic compressible nozzle discharge, including sonic choking. Reference: NASA Glenn Research Center, Mass Flow Choking (online source checked during this round). The nozzle law describes discharge, while isothermal storage describes the tank; these are distinct assumptions.
discussion.interpretation: Define `z = Max(p-patm,0)` bar, `pu = Max(p,patm)` bar, `ratio = Max(patm/Max(p,patm),rcrit)`, and `g = (gopen*(weight*(1-(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)+(1-weight)*(1-3*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**2+2*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)))` bar/s. The term `ain*flow` supplies pressure from the metered inlet. The term `(gopen*(weight*(1-(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)+(1-weight)*(1-3*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**2+2*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)))*(Max(p,patm)/patm)*sqrt(Max(2*gamma/(gamma-1)*(Max(patm/Max(p,patm),rcrit)**(2/gamma)-Max(patm/Max(p,patm),rcrit)**((gamma+1)/gamma)),0))*sqrt(Max(p-patm,0)/sqrt(Max(p-patm,0)**2+eps**2))` removes gas through an ideal isentropic restriction; `gamma` is the assumed ideal-air heat-capacity ratio, and `rcrit` prevents the pressure ratio from dropping below the sonic critical value. The factor `sqrt(z/sqrt(z**2+eps**2))` smooths the nozzle cusp at atmosphere and tends to unity well above `eps`. The tie `gopen = cap*sqrt(eps*patm/2)` sets the limiting small-overpressure restoring slope to `cap`. The heat-capacity assumption and choking transition come from gas physics, whereas the smoothing and `weight` stroke map are empirical. `-back*Min(p-patm,0)` restores numerical undershoots independently of valve position; it is not a real reverse-flow model.
discussion.origin: A compressible outlet law was included because observed absolute pressure extends above twice atmospheric pressure, where an ideal-air restriction can approach choking. Its pressure-ratio powers and critical-ratio clamp came from isentropic nozzle theory, rather than an algebraic search. Simple incompressible square-root and linear families were tried first. Unregularized nozzle simulations have a cusp at atmosphere; a pressure crossover scale and a bounded near-atmospheric slope were added for stable five-second integration. The two positive monotone cubic valve basis functions are empirical, and a third basis coefficient was removed after exploratory fits made it negligible. No symbolic search was used to generate the nozzle expression.
discussion.limitations: The effective inlet volume, valve area, discharge coefficient, temperature, bubble holdup and calibration cannot be separated from these two pressure/input trajectories. No flow-delay, thermal or actuator state is present. On an independently simulated validation trajectory, the earlier training-only fit gave RMSE 0.039679 bar; first-two-thirds fits gave fresh-initialized tail RMSE 0.027055 bar on training and 0.055087 bar on validation. Final all-data refitting gave training RMSE 0.026860 bar and validation RMSE 0.038294 bar; these last two are fitting diagnostics, not independent validation. Final one-step residual correlations with the next-minus-current inlet-flow change are -0.750 on training and -0.647 on validation, showing missing timing/dynamics that the autonomous single-state form cannot resolve. Alternative future-flow diagnostic fits reduced transition errors but were excluded because future inputs are not arguments. The fully open and sealed endpoints are extrapolated: training stroke spans approximately 10.31 to 92.41 %, validation 1.63 to 94.45 %. The subatmospheric term has no identified physical validity. Absolute pressures far outside the observed approximately 0.99 to 2.19 bar range, thermal transients, liquid-level changes and negative inlet flows are not validated. The fitted crossover scale is not small compared with typical overpressures, so the regularization materially affects the result and must not be represented as a harmless numerical epsilon. R1: `ain > 0`, so increasing `flow` always increases `dp`. R2: for `0 <= weight <= 1`, both cubic stroke basis functions are nonincreasing in closure, the pressure-drop discharge is nonnegative, and the subatmospheric term does not depend on closure; hence increasing `valve` cannot decrease `dp`, including in the implemented vacuum extension. R3: at `flow = 0` and `p = patm`, all terms vanish, with `patm = 1` bar. R4: for any not-fully-closed valve and `flow = 0`, `dp < 0` above `patm` and `dp > 0` below it, so atmospheric equilibrium is attractive. R5: at `valve = vfull`, the conductance is exactly zero, so for `flow >= 0` the derivative `ain*flow-back*Min(p-patm,0)` is nonnegative. No unexplained outlet leak remains at the sealed seat. These are structural properties, not conclusions inferred just from observed samples.
